elements.text: Pilot's failure to add fuel system icing inhibitor before the accident flights
Pilot's failure to take appropriate remedial actions (including diversion) after low fuel pressure and lateral fuel imbalance developed
Loss of control while maneuvering the left-wing-heavy airplane near the runway approach end
Accumulation of ice in the fuel system with initial concentration at the airframe fuel filter
Low fuel pressure state resulting from fuel system icing
Restricted fuel supply from the left tank due to ice accumulation
Development of a left-wing-heavy fuel imbalance
Fuel being drawn solely from the right fuel tank while left and right tanks received equal fuel via return lines
Pilot's failure to perform a complete preflight inspection to detect ice crystals, water, or fuel filter bypass indicator status
Pilot's failure to follow Pilatus Aircraft’s required procedures for flight operations with a fuel imbalance
Pilot's decision to divert later than necessary, resulting in a more severe fuel imbalance and deteriorating aircraft performance
Pilot's underestimation of the seriousness of initial fuel imbalance indications due to past experiences
Pilot was properly certificated and qualified
No evidence of preexisting medical or behavioral conditions affecting pilot performance
Airplane was properly certified, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of preimpact structural, engine, or system failures
Fuel system continued to provide fuel despite low pressure and degraded left-side performance
Airplane was controllable in static flight with the fuel imbalance
Passengers were not properly restrained
Excess passengers did not directly affect the outcome of the accident
Recommendation to improve fuel filler placards regarding icing inhibitors
Recommendation for FAA guidance on fuel system icing inhibitors
Recommendation for better crash protection via seat/restraint limitations
Recommendation for flight recorder systems capturing audio and images
